risks: Minimal: questionnaires and a home chair stand test already used in care, and interviews about experience. Risk of falls during home testing is managed by the camera check and a stable chair.
consent: Written or recorded verbal consent for interviews and for use of routine outcomes in the evaluation; declining does not affect access to either programme.
data: Routine outcomes extracted with a study number; interview recordings transcribed and deleted after checking; data kept on the hospital research drive for seven years.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: age, rurality, income, language and digital access shape who can use video. Interpreters, loaned tablets and telephone interviews are offered, and completion and outcomes are reported by age group, internet access and language.
effectiveness: The evaluation succeeds if it tells the hospital whether outcomes are in the expected range and which groups need an alternative to video.
efficiency: Uses routine data and 3 hours per week of staff time.
costs: Staff time and interpreter bookings within the service budget; four loaned tablets already owned.
grants: None needed; findings could support a regional application for digital inclusion support.
partnerships: Two patient partners with knee osteoarthritis, one of whom stopped the video programme, the hospital interpreting service and the regional library digital skills scheme.
rebPath: Approved by the research ethics board on 2026-09-19 (REB-26-0875) under TCPS 2 principles for the interview component; routine outcome use covered by the same approval.
limitations: No comparison group; non-completers may be hard to reach; interviews reflect those willing to talk.
summary: Approved minimal-risk evaluation with consent for interviews and equity built into sampling and reporting.
